title: Qman DirectPath authority entities
x-qmanInteroperableIntegerRange: Every JSON numeric integer is in -9007199254740991..9007199254740991 before canonicalization; wider values use schema-defined decimal strings.
description: Closed portable persistence schema for the DirectPath controller, host, assignment, lease, journal, quarantine, relocation, idempotency, audit, and outbox authority records. The schema fixes wire types and state vocabularies; target repositories may normalize these records across tables but may not weaken their authority or lifecycle semantics.

pidStarttime.description: Canonical unsigned decimal Linux /proc pid starttime ticks. A JSON string avoids implementation-dependent safe-integer truncation.

memberGenerations.x-qmanMapOrder: object keys are encoded by CANONICAL-JSON-V1; key set must exactly equal the canonical memberDeviceUids set for the covered scope

hostJournalUpperBound.description: A Host Agent fsynced acknowledgement that locally fences the exact operation lease before the global unstarted-reservation cancellation transaction. Sequence zero uses the deployment-fixed journal genesis digest.

qemuExistenceProof.description: Closed projection of a durable launch-journal/process-census proof. proofHash resolves to the complete immutable evidence artifact; a caller-provided assertion is not proof.

x-qmanCrossFieldRules: Every global mutation compares clusterId, leaderIdentity, controllerGeneration, authorityLeaseId, unexpired authority, and resourceVersion in one CAS
Expiry or replacement fences all new mutations from this authority but never revokes a BundleLease, consumes a ReleaseOwnershipGuard, or proves physical release
controllerGeneration and resourceVersion increase monotonically; a new leader or authority lease cannot reuse an earlier generation
[hostId,kernelBootId,hostEpoch,agentIdentity,agentGeneration,lastSnapshotEpoch,currentSnapshotContentHash] identifies exactly one signed current HostSnapshot
Within one [hostId,kernelBootId,hostEpoch,agentGeneration], lastSnapshotEpoch is monotonic and currentSnapshotContentHash changes only by the atomic current-pointer CAS to that exact signed snapshot
A kernelBootId or agent authority replacement increments hostEpoch and/or agentGeneration and requires a new signed current snapshot before ONLINE_COOPERATIVE
Only ONLINE_COOPERATIVE after completed boot, owner, backend, lease, quarantine, and journal reconciliation is schedulable; heartbeat or reachability alone never proves clean release
RECONCILING and UNREACHABLE retain every existing physical claim and reject new assignment, owner, release handoff, and relocation-target side effects not explicitly authorized by reconcile

x-qmanLifecycleRules: state is exactly FSM-OWNER-ACTIVATION; only its contract transitions are legal
APPLYING requires a live OWNER_TRANSITION operation lease for ownerGroupHash before the first member side effect
PENDING_REBOOT pins the exact identityManifestHash, requestSetHash, ownerGroupHash, expectedSnapshotEpoch, desiredOwner, and requestMode and never retargets by PCI ID
ACTIVE requires full-group owner/provider readback; rollback ambiguity retains the complete scope in QUARANTINED
state is exactly FSM-ASSIGNMENT; only its contract transitions are legal
A new execution attempt creates a new runId/runGeneration and may not retarget an existing run
ATTACHED is the only runtime-available state and requires one complete AssignmentManifest v2 plus matching backend, process, observed-plan, guest, IOMMU, DMA, and IRQ receipts

PREPARING reaches FREE without physical cleanup only through one complete ReservationCancelReceipt proving no Host Action Journal INTENT; after any host side effect, FREE requires atomic full-scope clean release
QUARANTINED retains all uncertain claims; FAILED is not permission to revoke leases or reuse a device
[runId,requirementId,ordinal] and bindingId are immutable for one run generation
The complete ordered binding set reserves, attaches, releases, revokes, or quarantines atomically with its AssignmentRun and BundleLease set
assignedIdOrNull is non-null only for a committed Dynamic runtime binding and is cleared in the same transaction that makes the run FREE; it is never a persistent selector
REVOKED cannot authorize a host action or QEMU launch; QUARANTINED retains deny and ownership evidence
memberDeviceUids is the exact complete exclusive attach group and exactly equals the key set of expectedMemberGenerations
scopeHash binds bundleId, ordered memberDeviceUids, expectedMemberGenerations, runId, ownerVmId, runGeneration, and hostEpoch
RESERVED, PREPARING, ATTACHED, RELEASING, and QUARANTINED all retain exclusive physical claims; TTL, controller expiry, process exit, or host loss never changes that fact
Only one atomic unstarted-cancel or full clean-release transaction may transition the complete canonical lease set to REVOKED
REVOKED cannot authorize any side effect; QUARANTINED retains claims and denies reuse until full-scope remediation

Within [hostId,hostEpoch,journalEpoch], sequence is gap-free and append-only and priorEntryHash equals the preceding entryHash; the genesis priorEntryHash is the deployment-fixed journal genesis digest
entryHash is the CANONICAL-JSON-V1 digest of the complete entry with entryHash omitted
The exact live typed OperationLease must match operationLeaseId, scopeHash, runIdOrIntentId, hostEpoch, and member generations before an INTENT is accepted
INTENT is fsynced before the first covered side effect; RESULT or COMPENSATION is fsynced after observation and references the corresponding receipt
The journal is recovery evidence only and cannot create, transfer, revoke, or free global authority

x-qmanCrossFieldRules: leaseSetHash is the CANONICAL-JSON-V1 digest of the complete ordered leaseBindings projection
Every leaseBinding belongs to exactly runId/runGeneration and its memberDeviceUids is complete for bundleId

hostJournalUpperBound is captured under the exact current host/hostEpoch/journalEpoch and operation-lease resourceVersion; its fsynced fence acknowledgement serializes against the local action executor, proves no INTENT for this run generation exists through sequence, and prevents any later INTENT under that operation lease

The referenced operation lease is ASSIGNMENT_PREPARE for the exact run/scope. Its active version, fence acknowledgement, controller generation, run generation, every lease id/version, every binding, and PREPARING run resourceVersion are compared; the operation lease becomes REVOKED and all reservations become REVOKED/FREE in one global transaction or none change
receiptHash is the CANONICAL-JSON-V1 digest of the complete record with receiptHash omitted
After any owner, driver, reset, VFIO, QEMU, or cleanup INTENT, this receipt is invalid and full physical clean release is mandatory

ENTITY-CLEAN-RELEASE-ACCEPTANCE.x-qmanAtomicAcceptanceRule: In one global repository transaction, compare receiptDigest, assignment/run identity, oldRunGeneration, sourceHostEpoch, expectedAuthorityResourceVersion, the complete expectedLeaseBindings and expectedLeaseSetHash; require the signed clean-release receipt is unexpired; revoke exactly the complete old lease set; advance the assignment/relocation authority to committedAuthorityResourceVersion = expectedAuthorityResourceVersion + 1; write this acceptance record, audit event and outbox; then commit. Any mismatch writes nothing.
ENTITY-CLEAN-RELEASE-ACCEPTANCE.x-qmanExactlyOnceRule: receiptDigest and idempotencyKey are globally unique. Replaying the same receipt returns this byte-identical acceptance; reusing either key with different canonical inputs is rejected. No target solve, FREE reuse or lease disappearance is authoritative without this record.
ENTITY-CLEAN-RELEASE-ACCEPTANCE.x-qmanDigestAndSignatureRule: acceptanceDigest is SHA-256(CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of this complete object with acceptanceDigest and signature set to null). signature is Ed25519 over ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/CLEAN-RELEASE-ACCEPTANCE/V1) || 0x00 || the same bytes using a non-revoked CONTROL_REPOSITORY_EVIDENCE key. acceptedAt must be no later than receiptExpiresAt.

x-qmanLifecycleRules: One generation covers the exact canonical transitive lease, bundle, member, reset, owner, and target-attempt scope; bundleIds and memberDeviceUids are never narrowed
An uncleared record atomically retains every applicable claim and deny index and blocks owner transition, solver, reserve, attach, release takeover, and partial remediation
A failed or ambiguous remediation creates evidence and leaves clearedBy/clearedAt null; it never deletes or partially clears the record

clearedBy and clearedAt become non-null together only in the same CAS that verifies a successful full-scope RemediationRun, exact generation/resourceVersion, current controller authority, and clean-release evidence
clearedAt is strictly after createdAt; historical cleared records remain append-only audit evidence
state is exactly FSM-QUARANTINE-REMEDIATION; only its contract transitions are legal

REMEDIATING requires one live QUARANTINE_REMEDIATION operation lease matching quarantineScopeHash, exact quarantine generation, host epoch, member generations, controller generation, and resourceVersion
A failed or unknown attempt returns to QUARANTINED, increments a future attempt, preserves the complete quarantine scope and claims, and records a closed reason/evidence
FREE requires complete identity, DMA/IRQ, IOMMU, reset/state, owner, lease, and member proof plus the atomic quarantine-clear CAS
state is exactly FSM-COLD-RELOCATION; only its contract transitions and pseudo-state expansions are legal
source identity, source assignment/run/assignedId/manifest, source run generation, source host, and source host epoch are immutable for one relocation generation

sourceCleanReceiptIdOrNull and sourceCleanFactVersionOrNull are both null or both non-null; acceptance consumes one signed receipt exactly once and atomically revokes the complete source lease set before TARGET_SOLVE
Each targetAttempt greater than zero has a new targetAttemptId, targetRunId, targetRunGeneration, and append-only audit history; at most one target lease set is active
targetAssignedIdOrNull, when present, differs from sourceAssignedId; source BDF and assignedId are never copied as target selection constraints

ATTACHED either represents the original untouched source assignment before relocation side effects or a fully committed target with non-null target assignment, assignedId, and manifest; a target commit starts a later relocation only with a new relocationGeneration
STOPPED_UNSAT and HOST_UNREACHABLE are durable quiescent failure states, not success; pre-clean source loss retains every source claim and never permits target reservation
TARGET_ROLLING_BACK reaches STOPPED_UNSAT only after complete target clean release; cleanup ambiguity quarantines the complete target scope without altering sourceCleanFactVersion
[scope,idempotencyKey] is a permanent natural key for the retention window
The first accepted canonical requestHash fixes exactly one runId; the same key and hash replays that run/result and a different hash is rejected with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED
COMPLETED is monotonic and its responseHash is immutable; retry or client timeout never creates a second run, lease, or physical side effect
Expiry only permits retention cleanup after every referenced operation, audit, lease, and recovery obligation is independently durable; expiry is never cancellation or release authority
Only ACTIVE authorizes the one exact leaseType, scopeHash, runIdOrIntentId, bundleIds, memberGenerations, hostEpoch, run generation or intent version, controller generation, and resourceVersion
The five leaseType values are non-interchangeable and every physical/reset/exclusive-domain overlap uses one shared conflict key
The executor revalidates the live ACTIVE row and sealed capability before the first covered side effect and binds it to an fsynced Host Action Journal INTENT
CONSUMED and REVOKED never authorize or resume a side effect; replay returns the durable prior result or requires a new lease
QUARANTINED never authorizes normal side effects and retains the complete scope's deny/claim effect until full-scope remediation
Lease loss, ambiguity, controller expiry, or host loss after a side effect enters reconcile and retains/quarantines claims; it never implies clean release
operationLeaseId resolves to one live RELEASE OperationLease whose exact scope, run, host epoch, run generation, holder controller generation, and resourceVersion match this guard

leaseSetHash binds the complete ordered leaseBindings including every exact leaseVersion, bundleIds, memberDeviceUids, and current member generations; bundleIds exactly equals the canonical bundleId projection of leaseBindings and no subset guard exists

qemuPidStarttimeOrNull is null exactly for DURABLE_NEVER_CREATED; EXIT_PROVEN requires the exact managed-process starttime as a canonical decimal string, and proofHash binds that identical value plus pid, run, host epoch, launch journal, pidfd/exit observation, descriptor census, and observation time
Only ACTIVE authorizes ordered stop/teardown and excludes every new launcher/open path, owner transition, reset by another run, relocation target use, and quarantine clear
CONSUMED never authorizes another side effect and exists only after one atomic full-scope clean-release commit
QUARANTINED retains all claims and deny effects; cleanup uncertainty cannot consume the guard, revoke a lease, or make any member FREE
QEMU-owned VFIO or IOMMUFD descriptors are not retained cross-process; backend release contexts are freshly reacquired under the live guard and exact qualified profile
Events are append-only CANONICAL-JSON-V1 records ordered by aggregateType, aggregateId, aggregateVersion and chained by priorEventHash; the genesis digest is deployment-fixed
aggregateVersion equals the authoritative aggregate version committed in the same transaction and may not be fabricated by an asynchronous logger
correlationIds is a canonical set containing every applicable command, idempotency, VM, run, assignment, lease, guard, host, relocation, and evidence correlation
An audit event records a decision but never substitutes for an OperationLease, BundleLease, ReleaseOwnershipGuard, receipt, signed evidence, or state CAS
The initial PENDING row is inserted in the same transaction as the exact aggregate transition and aggregateVersion
Delivery is at-least-once; consumers deduplicate by [outboxId,aggregateType,aggregateId,aggregateVersion] and verify payloadHash
PUBLISHED requires durable broker/consumer-acceptance evidence and publishedAtOrNull no earlier than createdAt
FAILED is not PUBLISHED, keeps publishedAtOrNull null, and cannot be interpreted as delivery success; a retry increments attempt and resourceVersion under CAS
Outbox publication does not confer authority and cannot repair or advance an aggregate state

x-qmanGlobalRules: Every object is closed: a target extension requires a versioned portable schema change, not an ignored column or open JSON member
All timestamps use TIMESTAMP-UTC-US-V1: UTC RFC3339 with exactly six fractional digits and literal Z
All generation, epoch, lease version, aggregate version, and resourceVersion values are integers greater than or equal to one and advance monotonically in their declared authority scope
All x-qmanSetOrder annotations are normative; a validator rejects non-canonical input order rather than sorting it before validation or hashing

Every mutable authority transition compares the current controller generation and resourceVersion plus every applicable host epoch, run generation, lease version, member generation, quarantine generation, state, and immutable scope hash
An expired, REVOKED, CONSUMED, FAILED, UNREACHABLE, or otherwise non-active authority never authorizes a side effect; uncertainty retains or quarantines the complete physical scope
No local journal, outbox, audit event, TTL, heartbeat, process absence, or controller fence can create, transfer, revoke, or cleanly release physical ownership
